title: Package registry: after a restart the server serves an older manifest than the last overwrite re-install (rollback, or several writes within one second)
body:
qa#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibw6yXcLi9aRRBpPT4W

## Reproduction (fresh file DB, admin session; reproduced twice at 8e3d4a54 on a scratch app copy and once at 18.3.0 on the stock showcase)

1. `POST /api/v1/packages?overwrite=false` body `{manifest:{id:"com.example.qa-rollback", name:"QA rollback", version:"1.0.0", scope:"project", type:"app"}}` → 201.
2. At least 1 s later, `POST /api/v1/packages?overwrite=true`, same id, `version:"2.0.0"` → 201.
3. At least 1 s later, `POST /api/v1/packages?overwrite=true`, same id, `version:"1.0.0"` (rollback) → 201. `GET /api/v1/packages/com.example.qa-rollback` → version **1.0.0**; the list shows one row, 1.0.0.
4. Restart the server on the same DB. `GET /api/v1/packages/com.example.qa-rollback` → version **2.0.0**.

Same-second variant: three installs/overwrites 1.0.0 → 2.0.0 → 3.0.0 within one second serve 3.0.0 live and **1.0.0** after the restart.

## Expected vs actual

The manifest served after a restart equals the last one written and served. Actually the restart silently reverts it.

## Mechanism (read, not changed)

`sys_packages` is keyed `(id, version)`, and get/list pick "latest" by `ORDER BY created_at DESC` / `MAX(created_at)` (`packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts`). `created_at` has whole-second precision, and the upsert keeps an existing `(id, version)` row's `created_at` (`package-table.ts`). So re-installing a version the package already had never becomes latest, and same-second rows tie.

## Not a regression

18.3.0 (83d7e4ae) gives the same answer to steps 1–4 (1.0.0 live, 2.0.0 after the restart).
